import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 7

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/7](https://www.erdosproblems.com/7)
-/

namespace Erdos7

open Set

/--
Is there a covering system all of whose moduli are odd (and greater than 1)?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_7 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (C : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ), ∀ i,
      ¬ C.moduli i ≤ Ideal.span {2} ∧ C.moduli i ≠ ⊤ := by
  sorry

end Erdos7

reformulations.difference: The statement uses ideal cosets in StrictCoveringSystem ℤ and the condition ¬ C.moduli i ≤ Ideal.span {2}, rather than explicitly using congruences modulo distinct odd integers greater than 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every ideal of ℤ has a unique nonnegative generator m. The covering-system fields excluding ⊥ and ⊤ force m > 1. The containment mℤ ≤ 2ℤ is equivalent to 2 ∣ m, so its negation is exactly oddness. Injectivity of the ideal moduli is equivalent to distinctness of their positive generators, and {r} + mℤ is exactly the congruence class r modulo m. The finite index type and unionCovers field express a finite family covering every integer. Conversely, any such ordinary congruence covering constructs the required StrictCoveringSystem. The additional explicit condition C.moduli i ≠ ⊤ is redundant but harmless. This full equivalence, including preservation of an arbitrary yes/no answer slot, was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: Checked the sole declaration and its dependent definitions. The cited source still labels problem 7 open; the solved odd-squarefree variant mentioned there is not asserted in this file. Scratch proofs use no sorryAx. Boundary checks exclude empty and singleton coverings, zero and unit moduli, and even moduli; computations on natural moduli 0 through 11 accept exactly 3, 5, 7, 9, and 11. A standard distinct covering was also constructed to verify that the underlying structure is nonvacuous. No repository files were edited.
